newsitem.title: UK: OPEC output steady in Sept at 25.86 mbpd - survey.
newsitem.headline: OPEC output steady in Sept at 25.86 mbpd - survey.

text.p: Buoyant oil prices kept most Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries' members at full blast in September and encouraged some producers to sneak out a few extra barrels, a Reuter survey found.
Most OPEC countries continued to flout self-imposed quotas at a time when rising world oil demand has allowed refiners to suck in all the extra supplies they can find.

But the handful of Middle East OPEC members with extra capacity -- Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates and to a lesser extent Kuwait -- so far have not been enticed in to raising output significantly, the survey found.

OPEC wellhead crude output in September was just about unchanged at 25.86 million barrels per day (bpd) from a revised 25.87 million in August, the survey of OPEC, industry officials and analysts found.

Slightly lower production from OPEC's biggest supplier Saudi Arabia along with Nigeria balanced higher volumes from Qatar and Iran but volumes still easily outstripped the group's 25.033 million bpd collective ceiling.
Iraq's prolonged absence from world markets, following postponement of May's U.N. oil-for-food exchange, leaves tight markets without an expected 600,000 bpd of extra fourth quarter supply.

OPEC's three excess-capacity Middle East suppliers have not been tempted to make up the difference, but analysts said an extra cargo or two might be expected to slip in to thirsty Atlantic Basin markets. "The no-show of Iraqi oil during the fourth quarter will be felt by the market," said Washington's Petrofinance Corp. "Only a fraction of this amount will be replaced elsewhere. We believe that the three producers with extra capacity will market one or two extra cargoes a month."
Iranian, constrained by capacity, forced exports to a higher 2.67 million bpd in October for production 70,000 bpd over quota at 3.67 million, monitors said.
Qatar also managed to squeeze output higher from foreign company operated fields to reach 490,000 bpd compared to its 378,000 bpd quota.
Kuwait stayed a little over quota at 2.07 million.
Saudi Arabia pumped a slightly lower 8.05 million bpd from the wellhead, versus 8.09 million in August, keeping the kingdom's average production at some 8.13 million for the year so far.
Nigerian output was hampered a little by problems with its small Bonny Medium stream but the West African producer was able to stay well in excess of its 1.865 million quota at 2.03 million bpd.
Venezuela continued to lead the pack of OPEC quota violators at a steady 3.12 million bpd in September, massively over an official 2.359 million quota.
The Reuter survey seeks a best estimate of wellhead flows in OPEC countries based on the views of officials, industry monitors and analysts inside and outside member countries.
OPEC quotas are based on supply to market, defined to exclude movements to, but not sales from storage.
